correctness.rationale: Source eqs (2.4),(2.5) give exact Phi=1−nu²/x²+(J'/J)² and xPhi'/2=1−(1+xJ'/J)Phi; source strict convexity gives unique nodal minimum. DLMF 10.19.6–7 and 10.41.10 yield uniform smooth cos-even/sin-odd Debye expansion for t=x/nu in compact t>1. Stationarity localizes phase theta=npi+O(nu^-1), and coefficient matching yields delta=−(9t²+22)/(24(t²−1)^{3/2})+O(nu^-2), hence rescaled location t−t(9t²+22)/[24nu²(t²−1)²]+O(nu^-4). The exact quotient and log-derivative yield beta=1−t^-2−(9t²+10)/[12nu²t²(t²−1)²]+O(nu^-4). Six numerical samples and rational algebra check reproducibility but do not replace proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is a uniform two-term asymptotic when n and positive real Bessel order nu grow at comparable rates. The nearest published comparison instead fixes mu and sends n to infinity, with a mu-dependent remainder, and explicitly does not treat simultaneous growth. The 2026 source proves uniqueness and monotonicity, not the ratio-dependent asymptotic profile or explicit 9t^2+22/9t^2+10 corrections. The older primary works give inequalities and distinct unnormalized-extremum statements. Source full-text sections and actual semantic searches were compared by logical implication, not title only; no covering statement was identified. Residual risk is an unindexed derivation elsewhere.

value.rationale: A uniform two-parameter crossover is the natural quantitative missing region between fixed-nu large-index and fixed-n large-order limits for sharp nodal Turán constants. The continuum of nontrivial limiting values is an exact interior scaling classification, and the explicit second-order corrections resolve both the sharp constant and optimizer location under the same quantifiers. Those facts are useful for comparing Bessel inequalities across concurrent order/index changes and are not arbitrary parameter substitution or a known table entry.
